messages.subject: Weird parameter estimates....
parts:
So I'm attempting to replicate a longitudinal panel model that was also done in MPlus as our project is switching to R. (yay!) However, not only am I getting different numbers than the MPlus model, I'm getting out of bounds parameter estimates. Note that I can't correlate the residuals of w3access and w4ladder as they are not the same constructs.

Here is my code:

aim2.model <- '
  # measurement model.
    w3fin =~ NA*w3income + w3strain + w3access
    w4fin =~ w4income + w4strain + w4ladder
    w3alc =~ NA*w3alc1 + w3alc2 + w3ex1 + w3ex2
    w4alc =~ w4alc1 + w4alc2 + w4ex2 + w4ex2
  # regressions
    w4alc ~ w3alc + w3fin
    w4fin ~ w3alc + w3fin
  # residual correlations
    w3alc1 ~~ w4alc1
    w3alc2 ~~ w4alc2
    w3ex1 ~~ w4ex1
    w3ex2 ~~ w4ex2
    w3income ~~ w4income
    w3strain ~~ w4strain
    w3fin ~~ w3alc
    w3alc ~~ w4alc
    #constraining latent variance
    w3alc ~~ 1*w3alc
    w3fin ~~ 1*w3fin
'
fit3 <- sem(aim2.model, data = aim2model, missing = "ML")
summary(fit3, standardized = TRUE)

Here is the covariance matrix:
          w3incm w3strn w3ccss w4incm w4strn w4lddr w3alc1 w3alc2 w3ex1 w3ex2

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Weird parameter estimates....
parts:
What out of bounds estimate are you talking about?  If this is the model-implied covariance matrix, you can't tell whether there are out of bounds estimates very easily -- try cov2cor() to turn it into a correlation matrix, and see if there are any values that exceed [1, -1].

If this is the sample covariance matrix, you can do the same cov2cor() check, but you might have out of bounds estimates because you have missing data, IF this sample matrix is estimated using pairwise deletion (instead of extracting the ML estimate from lavaan). 
 
If the correlations among your variables are as low as they seem from the covariance matrix, I wouldn't trust results from any package, unless you have a very large sample size and use more items to identify your constructs, in order to compensate for the low communalities (see attached article for advice).  But it's hard to tell whether this is a problem from your (unstandardized) covariance matrix.  It's also worth noting that you have some wildly different variances among the indicators within each construct (e.g., 2.8 vs. 0.03, or 7.25 vs. 0.48).  That can cause problems, so you might consider rescaling your variables in some way to make their variances more similar.  I don't have a specific guideline, but certainly the variables with more than 10 times, and some close to 100 times, greater variance than other indicators would be problematic (although I'm not sure it's related to why you get different numbers in the two packages).  

It's also possible you still aren't specifying the exact same model in both packages.  Have you checked your degrees of freedom and number of parameters being estimated?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Weird parameter estimates....
parts:
How about these two lines, farther down:
 w3fin ~~ w3alc
 w3alc ~~ w4alc
The first of these seems to break the pattern that otherwise characterizes your syntax.
--Ed Rigdon

Good eye, Ed, although I think it's the second of those that is inconsistent/problematic.  The "w4" variables are both regressed on both of the "w3" variables.  So the exogenous "w3" variables should be correlated, and the endogenous "w4" variables should be correlated.  But the line "w3alc ~~ w4alc" is specifying a covariance path where there is already a regression path: "w4alc ~ w3alc", so it's not identified.

# regressions

    w3alc2 ~~ w4alc2

    w3ex2 ~~ w4ex2

w3alc ~~ w3fin

How about these two lines, farther down:
 w3fin ~~ w3alc
 w3alc ~~ w4alc
The first of these seems to break the pattern that otherwise characterizes your syntax.
--Ed Rigdon


Good eye, Ed, although I think it's the second of those that is inconsistent/problematic.  The "w4" variables are both regressed on both of the "w3" variables.  So the exogenous "w3" variables should be correlated, and the endogenous "w4" variables should be correlated.  But the line "w3alc ~~ w4alc" is specifying a covariance path where there is already a regression path: "w4alc ~ w3alc", so it's not identified.

I'm not seeing any out-of-bounds estimates, anywhere in your output.  When you request standardized results using "summary(fit3, standardized = TRUE)", you will get unstandardized results under the first column (labeled "Estimate"), estimates where only the latent variables are standardized in the 5th column (labeled "Std.lv"), and estimates where both the latent and observed variables are standardized (labeled "Std.all").  For comparison, see the results for excluding the "standardized" argument: summary(fit3).

So the regression parameter that is 1.417 is not out of bounds because it is not standardized.  The standardized solution for this estimate, and for all estimates in your model, are within bounds (see the far right column).

Terry
